answer.evidence: About nine layer-1 units (2, 4, 7, 13, 17, 21, 22, 26, 29) carry only small, unstructured weights (|w| < 35) and look untrained or dead. The trained units fall into two radially symmetric families. (a) Ring units (1, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 16, 27, 30): a strong positive annulus over rows ~5-18 and cols ~5-18, a negative centre at rows 10-13, cols 10-13, and a mildly negative far surround on both the left and right edges and along row 22. (b) Centre/surround units (0, 3, 5, 8, 14, 15, 18, 20, 23, 24, 25, 28, 31): a small positive core at rows 10-13, cols 10-13, a negative annulus, and a positive outer border; this family is roughly the negated ring pattern. Unit 19 is nearly uniform positive (about 50) except at the centre, so it acts as an overall brightness term. Layer 2 routes the families in opposite directions. u4 (W3 = +99) takes positive input from ring units 6, 9, 26 and 30, and negative input from units 14, 24 and 25. u9 (W3 = -98) and u12 (W3 = -69) take positive input from units 14, 18, 20, 24 and 28, and negative input from ring units 6, 10, 16 and 30. So a bright annulus drives the output toward class 1 (large), while a bright core with a dark annulus drives it toward class 0 (small). I searched for a compact off-blob patch whose weights share one sign across units and are not mirrored elsewhere. The left-edge clusters (rows 8-9 and 14-16, cols 0-3) are matched by similar values on the right edge (rows 8-16, cols 20-23) and along the top and bottom rows, so they read as part of the circular surround. A few isolated spike pixels (r1 c0, r3 c12, r20 c19) are single pixels rather than a coherent patch. No corner or edge marker stands out. I cannot fully rule out a weak dependence on background brightness through the positive border weights.
answer.main_feature: The model compares brightness in a mid-radius annulus (about 5-7 px from the centre) with brightness in the small central core and outer surround. A bright annulus means a large blob (positive logit); a bright core with a dark annulus means a small blob (negative logit).
